book_title: Skating Wild on an Inland Sea
subject_line: Two skaters on a frozen Lake Superior bay
email_body:
Dear Jean,

Skating Wild on an Inland Sea sends two children out early one morning onto a remote frozen bay of Lake Superior, and it reads like a book that could only come from someone who knows that shoreline from Thunder Bay. I would love to ask how much of that morning on the ice comes from your own winters, and how you and Todd Stewart worked out the balance of words and space.

The Author Ledger is an independent project featuring short Author Spotlights. Each portrait is developed through a few written questions, which you can answer at your own pace, and the full text is shared with you for review before publication.

Would you be open to taking part? No pressure either way.

Best regards,
The Author Ledger
hook_note: Skating Wild on an Inland Sea (Groundwood, 2023, illus. Todd Stewart): two children skate on a remote frozen Lake Superior bay; GG Award shortlist/win 2024; Thunder Bay/Lakehead ties (CBC, Wikipedia, author site via search).

book_title: The Dialogues: The Song of Francis Pegahmagabow
subject_line: Francis Pegahmagabow and the shape of The Dialogues
email_body:
Dear Armand,

The Dialogues follows Francis Pegahmagabow from home through the First World War and on to the making of the opera Sounding Thunder, moving between poems and lyric essays. That it won the Betsy Warland Between Genres Award seems fitting. I would be curious to hear why this life asked for a hybrid form, and how working alongside the opera shaped the book.

email_body:
Dear Suzette,

The Sleeping Car Porter keeps Baxter, a Black, closeted sleeping-car porter, on a single cross-country train in 1929, and uses touches of magic realism to bring a stretch of Black Canadian history into view. I would like to ask what drew you to the confined world of the train, and how you decided where the uncanny should press against the historical record.
